learning_outcomes.text: Manage databases to store and extract information: Relational databases and data modeling.
Understand the basic concepts of different models and technologies of non-relational databases (documental, column family, graph, etc.).
Use the corresponding languages (SQL, CQL, APIs, etc.) to update and extract information from databases from applications.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and structure of Database Management Systems.
T1: Architecture and functionality of Database Management Systems.
Conceptual design with the Entity-Relationship model, integrity constraints.
Relational databases: relational model, transactions, security and concurrency control, data languages (definition, modification and query).
T3: Relational databases. Relational Model. Relational Algebra and Calculus.
T4: Design and optimization of relational databases. Normalization and query optimization.
T5: Transactions, security and concurrency control.
P1. Creation, manipulation and querying of databases. Procedures and functions. Packages. Exceptions. Implementation of semantic constraints.
P2. Use of libraries for data access.
Non-relational databases: Basic characteristics, storage types. Graph, document, semantic DBs (RDF, OWL). Technologies for handling non-relational databases.
T6: Advanced databases. Data warehouses and multidimensional modeling.
P3. Creation, manipulation and querying of non-relational databases.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance / participation in seminars and tutorials (AP) - Part 4

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points must be achieved in Part 1 (theoretical exams) and Part 2 (practical exams). If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as: 0.4 * Part 1 + 0.45 * Part 2 + 0.1 * Part 3 + 0.05 * Part 4. If the minimums are not met in Part 1 or Part 2, the final grade will be the minimum of 4 out of 10 and the weighted average. To pass, the final grade must be at least 5 out of 10. For extraordinary calls, only Part 1 (50%) and Part 2 (50%) are considered, with the same minimum grade requirements; grades from ordinary call elements that met the 5-point minimum are carried over.
